html:
Victor Hugues was the agent of the French Republic who retook Guadeloupe from the British in 1794 and applied the law abolishing slavery there. He ruled the island until 1798.

He arrived with a small force and a guillotine, freed and armed the enslaved, and drove out the British. Hundreds of royalist planters were executed. Freed people were forced to keep working on the estates.

He sent agents and arms to stir up revolt on British islands, among them Fedon's rebellion in Grenada and the Second Carib War on St Vincent, and his privateers seized many American ships. Later, as governor of French Guiana, he restored slavery there in 1802, as Napoleon ordered.
